summary.headline: The Golf Committee approved paying annual Audubon dues and discussed next steps for irrigation, fencing, and safety measures for errant balls hitting neighboring homes.
summary.summary: Following Town Meeting approval of golf course warrant articles, the Golf Committee discussed next steps and administrative responsibilities for the course irrigation upgrade and Audubon International certification. The committee voted unanimously to approve a $950 invoice for annual Audubon membership dues from the golf revolving fund. Members also discussed fencing specifications, ramp and step safety at the clubhouse, winter parking lot access, and ongoing concerns about errant golf balls striking residences on Latisquama Road.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved minutes from its pre-Town Meeting session, scheduled its next meeting, and adjourned.
key_details: Pre-Town Meeting minutes were approved unanimously.
The next committee meeting was scheduled for December 1, 2026.

topics.title: Town Meeting follow-up, irrigation project, and Audubon certification
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the outcome of Town Meeting regarding golf course warrant articles and discussed the procurement and administrative process moving forward. The Community Preservation Committee liaison reported that town procurement is handling the contract for an Audubon International consultant and that conditions in the warrant article must be satisfied before funds are released. Committee members discussed clarifying the division of responsibilities between town administration and the committee.
key_details: Warrant articles for course improvements were approved at Town Meeting.
CPC liaison reported the CPC will review warrant article requirements at its meeting next week.
Town procurement is managing the contract for the Audubon International consultant.
The chair took an action item to confer with the town administrator regarding project leadership and responsibilities.
topics.outcome: Chair to confer with town administrator Mark Purple on project coordination.

topics.title: Audubon International membership dues invoice
topics.summary: The committee reviewed membership fees for Audubon International, noting that annual dues had increased from $500 to $950. After consulting with the town accountant on the billing workflow for the golf revolving fund, the committee voted to authorize payment of the new invoice.
key_details: Previous annual dues were $500, which had been approved at an earlier meeting.
New invoice for 2026–2027 renewal is $950.
Funds will be disbursed from the golf revolving fund through the Select Board office.
topics.outcome: Approved payment of the $950 invoice unanimously.

topics.title: Fencing and tree planting specifications
topics.summary: Members discussed defining specifications for golf course fencing and native tree planting so the town can issue requests for bids. Discussion centered on whether the committee or town facilities staff should write technical specifications such as wire gauge, pipe dimensions, and materials.
key_details: Course fencing specifications remain pending for procurement.
A committee member agreed to meet with facilities director Bill Cundiff to determine how to establish bid specifications.
Committee discussed checking with Audubon International for golf course fencing best practices.
topics.outcome: Committee member Kathy will coordinate with Bill Cundiff on fencing specifications.

topics.title: Revolving fund status, clubhouse ramp safety, and winter access
topics.summary: The committee discussed tracking the remaining balance of the golf revolving fund after accounting for roughly $100,000 committed to irrigation alongside fencing and tree costs. Members also discussed recent facilities repairs to clubhouse steps, slip hazards on the access ramp during wet or frosty weather, and whether the town can plow the parking lot and leave gates unlocked in the winter for recreational walkers and snowshoers.
key_details: Roughly $100,000 in revolving funds is committed to the irrigation project.
Clubhouse exterior deck steps were recently repaired by facilities staff.
Clubhouse ramp becomes very slippery when wet or frozen, raising safety concerns.
The course gate is customarily locked for the winter after Thanksgiving weekend.
Inquiry will be made to facilities manager John Parent regarding non-slip ramp treatments and winter lot plowing.
topics.outcome: Chair will obtain an estimated revolving fund accounting and consult John Parent regarding ramp safety and winter parking lot access.

topics.title: Mitigation of errant golf balls on Latisquama Road
topics.summary: Members discussed ongoing issues with errant golf balls hit from the 7th hole striking neighboring properties on Latisquama Road, damaging house windows, car windshields, and sunroofs. The committee debated various potential solutions, including significantly shortening hole 7, shifting the green farther from the road, or installing high netting, while acknowledging that netting could conflict with preserving mature oak trees.
key_details: One homeowner reported more than 500 golf balls hitting their property.
Previous adjustments included shifting tee boxes to change shot angles.
Town legal counsel previously advised the town cannot pay for private property damage caused by golf balls.
Proposed ideas included shortening hole 7 to approximately 100 yards, moving the green, or installing high netting near the property line.
topics.outcome: No formal action taken; the chair placed the issue on future meeting agendas for continued review.

votes.motion: Approve payment of $950 invoice for Audubon International membership dues from the golf revolving fund
